topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the topic of complement, framing its conceptual importance and setting expectations regarding its complexity.

topics.label: Fundamentals and Architecture of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts, nomenclature rules, and central biochemical mechanisms governing the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the three distinct recognition pathways converge on activating the complement cascade on target surfaces.

topics.label: Effector Functions of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream effector mechanisms triggered by complement activation to eliminate pathogens.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that protect host cells from unintended complement-mediated damage.

topics.label: Clinical Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the distinct disease manifestations and clinical presentations resulting from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the strategies pathogens use to circumvent complement-mediated destruction, highlighting Staphylococcus aureus as an example.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the complement lecture and previews the upcoming topic on the adaptive immune system.
